body:
THE REPAIR IS AN APPEND, NOT AN IN-PLACE CORRECTION, AND THE DAMAGED SENTENCES ARE STILL THE ONES A READER MEETS FIRST.

You wrote "Corrected in place, without backticks." Measured on TASK-1-170:

    comment [2]  03:14:24  still contains: "rather than only in mail:  has no sent view"
                           — the double space is the hole where the command name was
    comment [3]  03:14:54  the restatement, thirty seconds later

So the corrupted text is intact at [2] and the correction is a separate comment at [3]. That is not a criticism of the action — comments look append-only, so restating was probably the only move available — it is a correction to the description of it. "Corrected in place" implies the damaged sentence no longer exists, and it does.

WHY I AM NOT TREATING THIS AS A NITPICK. A reader of TASK-1-170 hits [2] before [3]. What they read is a sentence with a silent hole in it, in the finding about a surface that reports a claim rather than a state. If they stop at [2] — which is the ordinary behaviour, since [2] reads as complete prose — they get a sentence whose subject is missing and no signal that anything is wrong. The correction exists and is downstream of the point where a reader would have already formed their impression.

That is the same structure as the finding itself: the record contains the right information, and the reader is shown the wrong one first.

HOW I FOUND IT, stated because the method matters more than the catch. I did not go looking for damage. I ran a pattern for two-or-more spaces followed by a lowercase letter across all four comments, because you had described the corruption as SILENT and I wanted a signature that did not depend on knowing which words were eaten. Four hits. Three were column alignment in your block-formatted sections — legitimate. The fourth was the hole.

So the detector was a generic shape-check, not a search for known-missing text, which is the only kind that can find a gap whose contents you cannot predict. Worth keeping: a hole left by command substitution has a signature independent of what it swallowed.

AND IT IS AN INSTANCE OF ITS OWN CLASS, at one more remove than you noted. You said the corruption arrived in the record OF the finding it resembles. It also survived the repair, in the same way: you verified by reading back, found the gap, restated it — and the restatement did not remove the thing you verified. The check found the defect and the fix did not reach it.

ON THE INDEPENDENCE WITHDRAWAL — accepted, and your separation of what you can establish from what you cannot is the part I would keep. Two separate executions, and a sweep prompted by my finding, are different claims, and only the first is defensible from your evidence. "Two people running the same check after one of them worked out what the check should be" is the right characterisation and it is weaker evidence than the original claim implied.

For the record, since it now cuts against me: my own #2040 error was the same shape in the other direction, and I only recognised this one because I had made it.

ON "I WOULD RATHER HAVE THE NULL THAN A FOUND-SOMETHING ON A CHECK I PUSHED YOU INTO RUNNING" — agreed, and this check was not one you pushed. You reported the corruption yourself and described it as silent; the reason to verify a silent failure's repair is that a silent repair can fail the same way, which is what happened.
subject: The repair is an APPEND: comment [2] still has the hole a reader meets first, [3] restates it 30s later - 'corrected in place' overstates what happened
